# DATA PACK — ISRG COMPLETE RS2 v2.0 EQUITY ANALYSIS

# SECTION 0 — SCOPE & METHOD

**Engine selected: Two-stage Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) Discounted Cash Flow.** ISRG pays no dividend; a dividend-discount model is inapplicable. A multiples-based approach would merely embed the same market optimism this analysis must independently test. With no debt, FCFF ≈ FCFE, and an equity bridge (adding net cash) yields per-share value.

**Cash-flow definition chosen, stated explicitly.** I anchor FCFF to **GAAP operating income (which includes stock-based compensation as an expense)**, then add back D&A, subtract capex and changes in operating working capital. This is deliberate: the data pack states SBC is a real expense added back in OCF, and an owner-earnings figure that starts from OCF without subtracting it is overstated. Anchoring to EBIT prevents double-counting.

**Discounted value received date.** Cash flows are assumed received at fiscal-year end (each Dec-31). T0 is Aug-24-2026, so the first cash flow (FY2026, ending Dec-31-2026) is discounted by t = 0.353 years. Each subsequent year adds 1.0 year.

**Sources are labeled throughout.** `[Actual]` = company SEC filing or regulator. `[Estimate]` = secondary (consensus, web source). `[Assumption]` = my own judgment. `[Arithmetic]` = exact math on filed values

# FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

**VERDICT: AVOID — DO NOT BUY at T0 = $376.84.**

**Intrinsic value (base case): $230 per share.** The stock is priced **39% above** my fair value, and **15% above even my bull case** ($322).

**The decision rests on five legs:**

1. **The discount-rate reality.** At the vendor beta of 1.46 and a 4.7% risk-free rate, the strict CAPM cost of equity is 11.3%. Even granting this franchise a quality premium (10% WACC — my base), the stock remains deeply overvalued. The market has priced ISRG at an ~8% discount rate, which implies a systematic risk profile (beta ≈ 0.7) the data does not support.

2. **Growth is decelerating, and management has told us so.** FY2026 da Vinci procedure guidance of 13.5–15.5% is down from 18% (FY2025). US growth has slowed 14% → 12% within two quarters. GLP-1s are shrinking bariatric volume; ACA marketplace churn is deferring elective procedures; China tenders are soft. These are not hypotheticals — they are Q2-2026 reported facts. A 45x trailing P/E leaves no room for these known headwinds to worsen.

3. **The quality is real — and it is already in the model.** The 85% recurring revenue, net cash of $8.9B, clean negative accruals, 80% market share, surgeon-training network effects, and 33% terminal GAAP margin are all embedded. Even conceding every quality argument, the margin of safety is −39%. Quality at the wrong price is still the wrong price.

4. **The stock's 37% drawdown is not a bargain; it is repricing.** The drop from $604 to $328–377 simply walked the multiple from mid-60s to low-40s. This is where the bear case (GLP-1, ACA, China, tariffs, Hugo) and bull case (da Vinci 5 upgrade + international) now genuinely conflict — exactly when the margin of safety matters most. At $377, the market has already decided; I do not.

5. **Management's buyback at $439 is a countervailing signal, not a controlling value fact.** It proves conviction but not intrinsic value. It does not reduce the 11.3% CAPM cost of equity, nor does it change the decelerating procedure-growth math.

**What would change my mind and trigger a BUY:**

## SECTION 8 — COMPETITIVE POSITION

**Moat: WIDE.** Research brief (Section 11) summarizes strong evidence: ~80% market share; 11,710 installed systems; surgeon-training network effects (switching costs); 25.6% NOPAT margins vs Medtronic/Stryker at ~15%; 0.84x capital turnover vs 0.49x. **Corroborated by the pack directly:** gross margin 66%, 12-yr median operating margin 30%, zero debt, $5.7B in growth investments self-funded.

**Threats:** Medtronic Hugo and J&J Ottava have capital and distribution muscle; hospital capital budgets are constrained; FDA safety communication on curved-tip staplers (2026) is a genuine reputational overhang. The moat is durable but not immortal — this is why the terminal margin assumption fades to 32.5% in the base case rather than staying at the 2025 level of 29.3% (or the vendor’s quoted 33.6%) forever.

**Pricing power evidence:** Procedure growth 16% with system installs +12% and recurring revenue ~75% — the razor/razor-blade model is intact. Margin expansion guidance (+150-200bps in 2026) confirms pricing and mix are working despite tariff headwinds.

## SECTION 9 — BEAR CASE

1. **Competition:** Medtronic Hugo remains the #2 credible entrant; J&J Ottava has regulatory runway; both have balance sheets to subsidize capital pricing. ISRG’s 80% share is unlikely to survive a decade of hospital budget pressure.
2. **Procedure-growth deceleration is already visible:** FY2026 guidance of 13.5–15.5% vs. actual ~19-20% in 2025 — a 5pt guidance decline that spooked the market (stock −10.9%). The bull case depends on this deceleration *reversing*; history says guidance is conservative, but the trend is against it.
3. **FDA stapler safety communication:** Curved-tip stapler injuries; potential liability, remediation, or surgical-confidence damage. The pack’s research brief flags it; the earnings excerpt does not mention it (prepared remarks only — no Q&A held).
4. **SBC load:** 7.8% of revenue is the single largest non-cash drag in the model. If SBC rises toward 9-10% of revenue (post-DV5 comp grants), owner earnings compress further.
5. **Working-capital cycle:** 2023–2025 ΔWC averaged +$1.3B/yr. If the DV5 inventory build was structural (not one-time), the model’s 8%-of-incremental-revenue assumption is too kind, and the bear case goes below $117.

**Bear-case floor:** $117 = a 32% downside. The floor is not zero — the installed base and recurring revenue provide intrinsic cash-flow support. But the downside is real.
